land.text: Galilee and Peraea, Herod the Great's northern and eastern Jordan lands

predecessors.note: The judea dossier records the 4 BCE split with this slug as counterpart.

land.text: Galilee and Perea, turned over to Agrippa in the summer of 39 when Antipas was exiled

successors.note: A proposed slug for the kingdom of Herod Agrippa I (37-44, with Judea from 41), which no group has yet written.

capitals.name: Sepphoris
capitals.note: 'Antipas became tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, with Sepphoris as his capital, later moved to Tiberias.' The Antipas page says he rebuilt and fortified Sepphoris.

capitals.name: Tiberias
capitals.note: 'Tiberias, so named to honour his patron Tiberius, who had succeeded Augustus as emperor in 14 AD'; the page gives no founding year, so 14 is the earliest the move could be.

rulers.name: Herod Antipas
rulers.title: tetrarch
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign 4 BC - 39 AD'; the page notes that some scholars have 1 BC for his father's death.

correction.text: Galilee in the north and Perea in the south, 'separated by the region of the Decapolis'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; Cliopatria's Judea shape of -4..5 covers all of Herod's old kingdom). The gazetteer has no Peraea, so Gilead stands in for it (the judea dossier does the same): 17 cells of Galilee and 13 of Gilead. No page gives an area.

region.text: Galilee and Perea, the two parts of the tetrarchy, with the Decapolis between them

ledger.note: 4 BCE: Herod the Great dies and Antipas becomes tetrarch of Galilee and Perea. 'Antipas became tetrarch of Galilee and Perea, with Sepphoris as his capital'; 'Augustus largely confirmed the division of territory set out by Herod in his final will'. The Antipas page: infobox 'Reign 4 BC - 39 AD', Galilee and Perea held 'for 42 years'.

4 BCE: the tetrarchy is held at Augustus's confirmation of Herod's will, as a Roman client; the page does not use the word client but Archelaus got the title ethnarch 'rather than king' and Rome deposed him in 6 CE.

AD 14 or later: Antipas moves his seat from Sepphoris to Tiberias. The Herodian tetrarchy page: Sepphoris 'later moved to Tiberias'; the Antipas page: 'Tiberias, so named to honour his patron Tiberius, who had succeeded Augustus as emperor in 14 AD'. The page gives no year; 14 is the earliest.
39: Rome ends the tetrarchy. 'In the summer of 39, Antipas' money and territory were turned over to Agrippa, while Antipas was exiled.'
39: Galilee and Perea pass to Herod Agrippa I. 'Herod Antipas ruled Galilee and Perea until 39 CE.' After his exile, Galilee and Perea went to Herod Agrippa I.
39: Antipas is exiled to Lugdunum (Josephus, Antiquities; the Wars of the Jews names Hispania) and his tetrarchy ends.

wars.name: War between Herod Antipas and Aretas IV
wars.outcome: 'It is generally agreed that the war, in which Herod was defeated, occurred in 36, a year before the death of Tiberius'; the page says the fighting took place 'between 34 and 36'.
wars.note: The page names no land taken; no border change recorded.

certainty.note: No page gives the tetrarchy's boundaries; Galilee and Gilead stand for Galilee and Perea.

sources.note: The 4 BCE division, Augustus' confirmation, capitals, Philip 34, Antipas 39, Agrippa I.

sources.title: Herod Antipas
sources.note: Reign 4 BC - 39 AD, Tiberias, the war with Aretas IV (36), exile 39.

notes: Two pages (budget 2-5, no Cliopatria shapes). The tetrarchy is a Roman client state; the vassal pair names roman-empire as in the judea dossier (client convention). The year of the Tiberias move is not on the pages (14 is a lower bound). Successor 'kingdom-of-herod-agrippa-i' is written in this batch (Agrippa I 37-44, Judea added 41: Herodian tetrarchy page); the 39 loss names it as counterpart. The Antipas page gives 4 BC from Schürer and says other scholars have 1 BC. Region 'Peraea' is missing from the gazetteer (Gilead stands in); the Decapolis cities between Galilee and Perea are not carved out.
